metric: Router-level list price per model (prompt/completion/cache/reasoning; tiered overrides)
units: USD per token (raw); USD per M tokens (normalized)
caveats: Current state only, no official history; history exists only from our first snapshot. Router price may differ from any single host's price.

metric: Per-host list price, quantization, context, uptime (5m/30m/1d), latency/throughput (often null)
units: USD per token (raw); USD per M tokens (normalized)
model_or_workload: All models; one row per (model, host endpoint)
caveats: One sample per day: misses intraday changes; uptime/latency are point-in-time. Official FAQ says pass-through pricing with no markup (some third parties claim ~10%; unverified). Listed price only; no volume. Host set biased to OpenRouter's marketplace.

source: LiteLLM price file git history (BerriAI/litellm model_prices_and_context_window.json)
metric: Per-token list prices per model key (input, output, cache read/write, batch/priority/flex tiers, long-context tiers)
caveats: Community-maintained, so the commit date is not the effective date. Spot checks: o3 cut and DeepSeek Feb-2025 change caught within the right week; gpt-4o alias change lagged ~6 weeks; deepseek-chat shows an implausible 0.6/1.7 entry and a ~3.5-month lag on the Sep-2025 cut. Must be audited against Wayback before any event study. Key renames show up as removed+added. History before 2023-09 may sit under an older filename (not checked).
snapshot_path: data/litellm/price_changes.csv (commit SHAs are the snapshot pointers)

metric: Measured throughput per GPU, TTFT/TPOT/ITL/E2E percentiles, KV usage, power per config and concurrency; $/M from SemiAnalysis TCO
units: tok/s/GPU; s; W; USD per M tokens
model_or_workload: Open-weight models on Nvidia/AMD/TPU; vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM, Dynamo; single_turn and agentic_traces
caveats: Cost assumes 100% utilization at each concurrency point and owner TCO, not rental prices. Data terms of use not stated: check before republishing rows. Rows carry the image digest and recipe_fingerprint, so they're reproducible.
snapshot_path: data/inferencex/reference_runs.csv (row IDs, run URLs and configs only; metrics not republished until terms are checked)

metric: Revenue, cost of revenue, T&I (incl. server D&A ~$2.3bn), D&A, useful lives, PP&E
caveats: Server depreciation is in Technology and infrastructure, not cost of revenue, so reported gross margin excludes the main asset cost. T&I D&A is a rounded MD&A figure. Revenue is mostly committed contracts, not spot.

metric: Revenues, cost of revenues, D&A (separate line), segment revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, useful-life change
model_or_workload: GPU cloud (neocloud) plus Avride and TripleTen
caveats: Material weakness in fixed-asset controls (depreciation start dates). D&A not disclosed by segment. Server life is 4 years in FY2025, extended to 5 from 2026. The 20-F/A only adds Exhibit 97.1.

source: SWE-bench bash-only submissions (mini-SWE-agent v2.0.0): repo metadata plus public S3 trajectories and harness reports
metric: Per-call input (incl. cache read and write), cache-read, cache-write, output and reasoning tokens and USD cost; per-task resolved verdict
model_or_workload: SWE-bench Verified, 500 tasks x 13 submissions, one attempt each
caveats: Verified is contaminated, so success is inflated. One attempt per task, no seeds. Costs are API list prices via the submitter's route, not cost-to-serve. The gpt-5-2-codex folder duplicates gpt-5-2-high (excluded). Gemini-3-pro per_instance_details is wrong (harness reports used instead). Some providers don't report cache or reasoning tokens (left blank). Raw trajectories not stored; S3 ETag recorded per task.

source: SWE-rebench leaderboard (Nebius); data embedded in the swe-rebench.com page
effective_date: task windows from 2025-01 to the snapshot date
metric: Per model or agent and task window: resolved rate, SEM and pass@5 across repeated runs, cost per problem, tokens per problem, cached-token share
model_or_workload: Fresh GitHub tasks (decontaminated by date), multiple languages; 117 models and products (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Junie)
caveats: No licence stated for the results (the task set is CC-BY-4.0), so we store the extracted numbers with attribution, not the page. Scaffold and cost method per entry are not fully documented. How costs are computed for subscription products like Cursor is unclear [U]. The site's 0 means no data (stored blank). Small windows: about 100 problems.
